analysis: The only change in this PR is a documentation addition to docs/developer/test.md (head lines 1059-1072). It describes SDK 27.2 Date-comparison and weak-import release checks: scripts/test-check-date-comparisons.py, scripts/test-check-provider-weak-imports.py, scripts/check-date-comparisons.py, and scripts/check-provider-weak-imports.py run on built binaries in the release lane. No code, configuration, key handling, wire protocol, authorization, attestation, cache or storage behavior changes. No trust boundary or mitigation is altered. The text frames the checks as CPU-only and static, using nm/otool fixture lines from a DevNet build, and does not claim any physical, security or qualification result. Examined the rest of both units for context. The surrounding text in lines 457-1382 is unchanged and describes existing test lanes: cache storage (T-041), endpoint resumption and logout (T-053), add-on hold (T-059/T-060), App Attest dispatch (TB-011) and the watchdog (T-043). I saw no new attack surface. Unverified: the referenced scripts and the build.md anchor are outside the supplied evidence, so I cannot confirm they exist or behave as the docs describe. That is a documentation-accuracy question, not a security regression. Nothing in this PR needs a threat-model update.
